correctness.rationale: For every nonzero real symmetric trace-zero 3x3 matrix, diagonalize and scale (or negate) to A=diag(u,1−u,−1), 1/2≤u≤1. For uniform area on S², polar height z is uniform [-1,1] and independent of azimuth theta, and h_A>0 iff |z|<sqrt(c_u(theta)/(1+c_u(theta))) with c_u=u cos²theta+(1−u)sin²theta. Hence H(u)=E[g(1/2+(u−1/2)cos 2theta)], g(c)=sqrt(c/(1+c)), and opposite-sign branch has probability 1−H(u). Explicit g'>0 and g''=−(1+4c)/(4 c^(3/2)(1+c)^(5/2))<0 prove strict Jensen maximum H(1/2)=1/sqrt3, while pairing cos 2theta gives strict monotonic H down to H(1)=1/2 by exact arcsine integration. Therefore sharp p range [1−1/sqrt3,1/sqrt3], exact uniaxial equality classes and p=1/2 iff rank two; all intermediate values by continuity. Uniform −g''≥5/(16sqrt2) on (0,1] and Var(c)=(u−1/2)²/2 yield the advertised nonoptimal rigidity coefficient 5/(64sqrt2) by quantitative Jensen; the measure-zero nodal locus justifies p(−A)=1−p(A). Independent numerical quadrature validated the full spectral monotone pattern but not the universal proof.
